transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this medication-exception huddle to discuss the formulary exception request for oral fidaxomicin for our medically stable patient who's planned for discharge tomorrow. I understand the treating team has requested this because fidaxomicin isn't routinely stocked for discharge prescriptions. Before I can sign off on the final plan, I need to hear from each of you -- infectious disease, utilization review, and discharge nursing -- so we can make sure the dispensing plan is appropriate and safe. Could we start with infectious disease's clinical rationale?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: The patient has had a second confirmed episode in six months, so infectious-disease guidance supports fidaxomicin 200 mg by mouth twice daily for exactly 10 days rather than the routine alternative. I reviewed the result this morning, but the updated recommendation is not yet in the discharge note.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something important from utilization review. The payer has already approved fidaxomicin for this patient for exactly 10 days under authorization code FDX-6382, provided the hospital dispenses it before discharge. I received the approval notice directly but have not yet entered it into the utilization system.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag something from discharge nursing. The patient lives alone and cannot reliably open a standard child-resistant bottle, so we've arranged a unit-dose blister pack and a medication-teaching visit at exactly 16:30 tomorrow. I confirmed both details with the patient today, but they are not yet on the discharge task list, so we need to make sure the dispensing plan accounts for the blister pack format.
